problem.title: The state of the descent and the primordial spectrum
problem.source: T07, successor problem (5); T16, successor problem (5); T17, open directions 5 and 10; maintainer decisions of 23 and 26 October; the results of 31 October; the results and Leon's decisions of 1 November, including the premise question answered for the coupling and the pre-descent Kasner stage postulated; the deposit-state results and Leon's decision of 1 November recording the spectrum as the deposit's infrared datum; the criterion, ledger and Kasner scalar-sector results and Leon's decision of 10 November keeping no mechanism
problem.statement: As stored, the series has no mechanism for the measured primordial spectrum. With the descent at the origin and no inflationary stage, no mode at or below the pivot scale leaves the Hubble length after the descent; a passive deposit needs correlations over one comoving length, about $9.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the present Hubble radius, which the frozen point's geometry supplies, but a deposit set by the frozen point reads the observed modes as inside its horizon and gives the vacuum's spectrum. Find the descent's deposited occupation numbers $n_{k}$, or a source acting after the descent, that give the measured amplitude and index, or show that the series cannot supply them.
problem.why: It is the programme item the synthesis paper assigns to the capstone itself; it would give the series an observable at the origin, where its dating places the descent, and without it the dating has no account of the earliest correlations.
problem.known: The finite-range bound: a deposit whose correlations have range $R$ gives $\Delta^{2}(k) \le \tfrac{2}{3\pi}\langle\zeta^{2}\rangle(kR)^{3}$; the pivot lay outside the descent's Hubble length by more than $2 \times 10^{5}$ (at $1$ MeV) to $3 \times 10^{20}$ (at $10^{12}$ GeV) and never leaves it after entering, so a passive deposit with $\langle\zeta^{2}\rangle \le 1$ needs correlations over more than $460$ to $6.8 \times 10^{17}$ Hubble lengths of the descent, which is one comoving length, about $9.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the present Hubble radius, at every reheating temperature; a deposit of finite range at the Hubble or thermal length gives $n_{s} - 1 \to 3$; active sources after the descent are not covered, and their acoustic peaks disfavour them as a dominant source (\claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}). Attack line 1 is closed (proved, 26 October, under hypothesis (F), the reading that the late de Sitter stage of the observed $\Lambda$ is the frozen point's own field, which the dating takes as primary): a deposit correlated by the frozen point's stabiliser has range $|x_{d}|$, about $4.3$ present Hubble radii, beyond the requirement by more than $4.4 \times 10^{5}$ at every reheating temperature, but every observed mode has $k|x_{d}| > 2.7$ (about $960$ at the pivot), inside the frozen point's horizon at the descent, so every stabiliser-invariant Hadamard state of a field of the series reads as the vacuum there: $n_{s} - 1 = 2$ exactly for the conformal weight, and within $3 \times 10^{-6}$ of $2$ at the pivot for every field of the unitary series at leading adiabatic order, more than $480$ standard deviations from the measured value (\claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-geometry-reads-descent-as-vacuum}, with \claimref{synthesis.imported-de-sitter-invariant-hadamard-state-unique}). In the second reading of the join, the frozen phase ending at the descent with the scale factor continuous, the modes are inside by more than $7 \times 10^{9}$ and the conclusion is the same (\claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}). On the descent slice a correlator homogeneous of degree $-2\Delta$ gives $n_{s} - 1 = 2\Delta$: finite range gives $3$, the frozen point's invariant class $2$, and the measured index is a slice correlator growing with separation (degree $+0.0351$), further from the vacuum than scale invariance, so any mechanism must produce long-range order above the vacuum's, not merely long range. Stationary excitations do not reopen the route: members of the half-KMS family cool enough not to resolve the observed modes read as the vacuum, and hotter ones are thermal deposits of finite range (argued). What is left is the descent's deposited occupation numbers: against the vacuum's $\Delta^{2} \propto k^{2}$, the measured spectrum needs $n_{k} \propto k^{n_{s} - 3}$ on observed scales, and nothing in the series fixes $n_{k}$. Earlier results fix what the descent cannot be: under (L$_E$) occupations are conserved, so the I-state must be deposited, not relaxed to (\claimref{synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermalise-descent}); a sudden start gives a feature, not a tilt (\claimref{synthesis.sudden-descent-feature-not-tilt}); a cold mirror needs a non-equilibrium descent (\claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}). The charge and energy per charge of the same deposited state are the entries of op.pre-descent-theory. Results of 31 October. (i) A quasi-free deposit on the fermionic boundary-mode algebra is its vacuum plus shot noise, whatever its correlation range or partner placement; for the I-state, or any quasi-free deposit with at least one thermal species' number of quanta at thermal energies (energy spread $c_{k} \le 1.31$), the shot term at the pivot is below $10^{-77}$, while a sparse or energetically broad deposit is bounded only by $(3c_{k}k^{3}/2\pi^{2}\bar n)^{1/2}$, and the record does not fix its number of quanta since such a deposit would not conserve entropy; the bound is on the fermion modes' contribution to the contrast of the total density (\claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}). So attack lines 1 and 2 are closed for dense quasi-free deposits, whatever the placement of partners. (ii) Attack line 3 is closed for the stored chain's defects: the Pati-Salam chain has topologically stable $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ strings besides its monopoles, but under Premise (R), unless the chain's restoration temperature is below $0.0176\,v_{R}$, neither forms after the descent, and a deposited string network has $G\mu < 1.5 \times 10^{-15}$ and supplies less than $10^{-16}$ of the CMB temperature power at $\ell = 10$, an active source and not a primordial spectrum (\claimref{synthesis.pati-salam-chain-defects-cannot-source-spectrum}). (iii) The one geometry in the store in which modes leave the Hubble length, a Kasner approach to a wall, gives a massless minimally coupled spectator scalar, within an epoch, an exited spectrum of index between 2 and 3, tending to 3, with the leading power $k^{3}$ of a finite-range deposit enhanced by a squared logarithm (so not of finite range): no red tilt (\claimref{synthesis.kasner-approach-gives-horizon-exit-and-index-three}); fields with a dilaton or modulus coupling (the hidden direction's Kaluza-Klein fields among them) and the conversion of a spectator spectrum into the curvature perturbation are not covered. The open part is therefore: sparse or energetically broad quasi-free deposits; non-quasi-free deposits (classical mixtures, non-Gaussian entangled states such as the families sector's frozen vacuum of bosonic face modes, if it were deposited); and bosonic fields with occupations far above one. Results of 1 November. (iv) The conversion step is closed for Gaussian fields: a local conversion of a Gaussian field into the curvature perturbation, as in the curvaton and modulated-reheating mechanisms (\claimref{synthesis.imported-curvaton-and-modulated-reheating-coefficients}), cannot lower the field's index (the classical Hermite-rank result, \claimref{synthesis.imported-mehler-formula-hermite-rank-and-power-law-spectra}), so under (F) any field of the series read on the descent slice through the frozen point's invariant state gives an index of $2$ up to corrections of order $(k|x_{d}|)^{-2}$ on observed scales (\claimref{synthesis.local-conversion-cannot-redden-a-gaussian-spectator}). (v) On a Kasner approach whose hidden direction moves, a scalar whose action carries the hidden scale to the power $\lambda$ with $|\lambda - 1| \le 2$, which covers every scalar the stored content supplies, is blue: at every Kasner point at least one observed axis has index at least $1$, and with equal observed exponents every axis does; the towers' u(3) vector zero modes are blue too (\claimref{synthesis.kasner-hidden-scale-coupled-scalars-stay-blue}). The gravitational field's off-diagonal modes and curvature-coupled scalars are red only anisotropically, with indices spreading by at least $4$ between axes against a statistically isotropic record (\claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-isocurvature-and-isotropy-bounds}), or, with equal observed exponents, through a curvature coupling $\xi_{R} \in [1.5225, 1.5481]$ fitted to the measured tilt; the Kaluza-Klein vector's field strength is blue, index at least $1$ (\claimref{synthesis.kasner-approach-coupled-modes-reach-measured-tilt-only-by-a-fitted-curvature-coupling}). (vi) By Wands' duality (\claimref{synthesis.imported-wands-duality-of-perturbation-spectra}) the stored Kasner index $3$ sits at the self-dual point, the stiff fluid; the contraction dual to the measured tilt needs $w = -0.0029$, which nothing stored supplies; an ekpyrotic contraction needs $w > 1$, and the stored walls stop at $w = 1$ (argued). (vii) Thermal fluctuations with an area-law heat capacity, converted as in string-gas cosmology (\claimref{synthesis.imported-string-gas-thermal-spectrum-and-conversion}), give $n_{s} = 1$ exactly at fixed temperature, eight standard deviations from the measured index, and with a heat capacity at most the area entropy their amplitude falls short by about ten orders or more at any temperature of the window under Premise (R), or at the frozen point's horizon temperature under (F) (\claimref{synthesis.holographic-thermal-fluctuations-fall-short-in-the-descent-window}). Conformal cyclic cosmology and the no-boundary state reduce to stored results (argued). (viii) Under the charge reading and the mirror's deposit law, a classical modulation of the deposit is adiabatic only along a local time shift of the one descent (\claimref{synthesis.adiabatic-deposit-modulation-is-a-time-shift}): a modulated deposit can carry the spectrum only as a field of delays of the one descent, which still meets the finite-range bound, and a Gaussian delay field read through the frozen point has index about $2$. So the classical-modulation escape is closed for Gaussian modulators. The open part is therefore: a red or non-Gaussian modulator; the amplitude; sparse or energetically broad quasi-free deposits; bosonic fields with occupations far above one; and the couplings the store does not fix (below). Premise question, answered for the coupling (results and Leon's decisions of 1 November). Write $\xi_{R}$ for the curvature coupling, to keep it apart from the D-term level $\xi$ of the weak scale (\claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}). At tree level no curvature coupling the series fixes reaches the window: the stored actions give $\xi_{R} = 0$, and the mass-weight dictionary read off the Einstein region with the frozen point in its stored form gives $\xi_{R} = -w/6$ with the transport's Thomas operator or $\xi_{R} = 0$ with the field-space connection. Which connection builds the Thomas operator off Einstein regions is left unrecorded by decision; neither reading reaches the window. The twelve values the series fixes (the largest $\tfrac12$) give an index of at least $3 - \sqrt{3}$ at the isotropic disk point, the only Kasner point the store fixes at which a coupling acts, and at least $3 - \sqrt{7}$ with the stored hidden-scale weights; the window needs a real weight below $-9$, outside both unitary series, and the own-scale reading, which drops the field-space premise, reaches it only for a principal-series scalar with $m^{2}/H^{2}$ between $18.27$ and $18.58$, which no stored field has (\claimref{synthesis.tree-level-curvature-couplings-stay-blue-at-the-isotropic-kasner-point}). Couplings the store does not fix remain open: loop-level couplings (a coupling of an interacting scalar runs, and the stored zero is not stable under renormalisation), and a periodic Wilson-line term $R\,V(W)$ of the holonomy, gauge invariant where a local $A_{y}^{2}R$ is not, which with the hidden-scale weight would need an effective coupling of about $0.856$ to $0.882$. The tilt-matching coupling $\xi_{R} \in [1.5225, 1.5481]$ is a free parameter of the series, not adopted. On the Kasner data: modes of every Bessel order leave the Hubble length only while an approach contracts toward its wall, the expanding branch fixes no state at its wall, and every stored Kasner wall except the flat Milne points is a curvature singularity; so, with the descent at the origin and the descended phase expanding from it (argued), a Kasner source needs a contracting metric stage before the descent and a rule carrying its state into the descended phase (\claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching}). By Leon's decision of 1 November both are postulated, (P1) (\claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-contracting-kasner-stage-premise}) and (P2) (\claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into-descended-phase-premise}), with their tension with the dating's pre-metric reading (\claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}, a conjecture) recorded and not resolved. They fix no Kasner exponents, and they still do not supply the tilt: granting both, the tree-level couplings above stay blue. They were not adopted in order to obtain a spectrum, and the series records no mechanism for the measured spectrum, no mechanism for its amplitude or its index. The spectrum as the deposit's infrared datum (results and Leon's decision of 1 November). Relative to any homogeneous Hadamard reference state of a scalar field on a spatially flat Robertson-Walker field, the Hadamard condition leaves the amplitude and the index of the spectrum free on every bounded band of scales: pure squeezed states reach every positive ratio to the reference spectrum there, at the price $n_{k} \ge (\sqrt{\rho_{k}} - 1/\sqrt{\rho_{k}})^{2}/4$; for the conformally coupled field a Hadamard state allows a power-law ratio on no band unbounded toward short scales (its energy moments are finite), and a homogeneous dilatation-invariant Hadamard state is the vacuum; for slice fields of nonzero mean a red or scale-invariant law on no band reaching $k = 0$ (the infrared divergence of Ford and Parker, \claimref{synthesis.imported-ford-parker-infrared-divergence}), while a blue law may reach it (\claimref{synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands}). Under the adopted premise that the deposit is Hadamard on a Cauchy collar of the descent (\claimref{synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise}) the spectrum is therefore recorded as the deposit's infrared datum: band data (amplitude, index and shape on the observed band) plus two scales, $k_{\mathrm{IR}}$ and $k_{\mathrm{UV}}$, between which a red band must lie, neither fixed by the Hadamard condition. That $k_{\mathrm{UV}} \sim 1/\tau$ for a descent smooth on a time $\tau$ is argued, not proved; a sudden or kinked descent has no such end and is not Hadamard (\claimref{synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-vacuum-and-non-smooth-descents-are-not-hadamard}). The fermionic deposit cannot carry the spectrum (occupations at most one, and the shot term below $10^{-77}$ at the pivot for a thermal-density deposit), so band data that carry it would have to be bosonic. This locates the spectrum among the deposit's free data; it is not a mechanism, and the series still records no mechanism for the measured spectrum. Results and Leon's decision of 10 November: the position is kept, no mechanism; the spectrum stays free initial data, the deposit's infrared datum, and no premise is adopted for it. What was examined. (a) The criterion: every stored mode equation on the primordial spectrum has one form, with friction excess $f$, curvature or mass term $\kappa$ and axis exponent $P$, and its exited spectrum is red exactly when $f^{2} + 4\kappa > 9(1 - P)^{2}$; on isotropic power laws that is $p > \tfrac23$, which the unit trace of the cited Kasner walls excludes for a minimally coupled field, so a red index there must come from the field's own weight or coupling (\claimref{synthesis.red-tilt-criterion-on-power-law-stages-and-the-index-ledger-of-the-stored-sources}(i)-(iii)). (b) The ledger: the cross modes, the hidden-scale weights, the Kaluza-Klein vector, the twelve tree-level curvature couplings, the weights of the frozen phase and the stages of the descended phase, each with its closed margin (clauses (iv)-(vi) there). Item (vi) above is now computed, not argued: on a contracting power law read as a fluid of pressure ratio $w$ the index is $12w/(1 + 3w)$, and the measured centre is $w = -0.0029$. (c) The Kasner scalar sector: at the isotropic point of the scalar disk the wall's own scalar, with the lapse and shift it forces, obeys the spectator equation of order $0$, and under the hypothesis of the stored adiabatic vacuum with a normalisation independent of $k$ the comoving curvature perturbation has a local index in $[2, 3]$ (\claimref{synthesis.scalar-sector-at-the-isotropic-scalar-kasner-point-obeys-the-spectator-equation}). So at that one point the stored blue index is the index of the curvature perturbation and not a property of a spectator or of the time slicing; the conversion left uncovered in (iii) above is closed there and nowhere else (anisotropic points of the disk are open). (d) Examined and not candidates (argued; none has a stored mode equation on a slice): the frozen point's moduli, its norm and point at infinity, which have no local mode and under the promotion one global pair supported at $k = 0$ (\claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}, \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}, \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}(iv)); the towers' pair channel, stored as one shell with no spatial mode, which if promoted to a field has a shift symmetry forbidding both a mass and a curvature coupling and is then the minimally coupled row or the de Sitter row at weight $0$; the towers' density-wave bosons on a null generator, for which no map from the generator to a slice is stored and uncorrelated generators give a blue index on a slice; and the horizon arrays and the de Sitter mode count, independent fermion modes whose contribution is the white shot noise of (i) above with the amplitude shortfall of (vii). These four are not to be reopened without a new stored structure. The corrected statement: no stored mode equation gives an index within three standard deviations of the measured one on three observed axes alike without a number chosen for that purpose. It is not true that none is red: the Kaluza-Klein transverse potential at the vacuum end $p = \tfrac12$, a point the store's own fields reach, has index $-1$ with no chosen number, far too red, while its field strength there has index $+1$. Status of the survey: argued. It is a pattern search of the formal levels with reading, not an audit of every derivation, and five stored results on the index are outside the ledger because they are not mode equations of that form: the thermal reading with an area-law heat capacity (\claimref{synthesis.holographic-thermal-fluctuations-fall-short-in-the-descent-window}), the sudden descent (\claimref{synthesis.sudden-descent-feature-not-tilt}), the band data of a Hadamard deposit (\claimref{synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands}), the local conversion of a Gaussian field (\claimref{synthesis.local-conversion-cannot-redden-a-gaussian-spectator}) and the joint condition on one curvature coupling (\claimref{synthesis.no-single-curvature-coupling-serves-the-sakharov-zero-and-the-kasner-tilt}). The rule for a future match (argued): the parameter-free rows already tried number about two dozen, with indices spread over an interval more than a hundred times wider than the three-sigma window, and the store already holds several one-parameter families that reach the window with certainty (the curvature coupling, the exponent of the Kaluza-Klein potential, the temperature exponent of the thermal reading, the pressure ratio of the dual contraction, the exit epoch of a dust contraction with the constant); so a match of the index alone by one more stored structure carries no evidential weight. A future index match counts only with a second number, the amplitude or the running, obtained from the same structure with no further chosen number.
attack: Test whether a red or non-Gaussian modulator of the deposit can carry an occupation law $n_{k} \propto k^{n_{s} - 3}$ on observed scales, compatible with the descent's one-way conditional expectation and with the mirror's cold deposit from the same event: the modulation must be a field of local delays of the one descent (\claimref{synthesis.adiabatic-deposit-modulation-is-a-time-shift}), and a Gaussian modulator read through the frozen point's invariant state is excluded (\claimref{synthesis.local-conversion-cannot-redden-a-gaussian-spectator}); a non-Gaussian deposited state, or a state other than the frozen point's, is what remains. Compute the amplitude for any candidate.

Decide whether any deposited quanta are bosonic fields outside the CAR algebra, with occupations far above one (the Higgs, the families sector's face modes). The coupled Kasner modes are decided: blue at tree level for every coupling the series fixes, red only anisotropically or through the free tilt-matching coupling $\xi_{R}$; the pre-descent Kasner stage is postulated as (P1) and (P2) and supplies no tilt. Decide whether a loop-level coupling or the Wilson-line term $R\,V(W)$ is fixed by the series, without fixing either in order to supply a spectrum.
Bound sparse or energetically broad quasi-free deposits: say what fixes their number of quanta when the deposit does not conserve entropy, and whether the record excludes them.

The infrared datum: find what in the series fixes the band data and the two ends $k_{\mathrm{IR}}$ and $k_{\mathrm{UV}}$ of a Hadamard deposit (the descent's duration as the candidate ultraviolet end), without fixing them in order to supply a spectrum.
problem.success: A mechanism in the series for the measured amplitude and index, with a computed $n_{s}$ to set against the measured value; or a proof that the series cannot fix the deposited occupation numbers and that no post-descent source of the series can supply the spectrum, settling the problem negatively.

entities.title: A finite-range descent deposit cannot seed the measured amplitude
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: A finite-range deposit has $\Delta^{2}(k) \le \tfrac{2}{3\pi}\langle\zeta^{2}\rangle(kR)^{3}$; with no horizon exit after the descent the pivot lay outside the descent's Hubble length by more than $2 \times 10^{5}$ to $3 \times 10^{20}$, so the measured amplitude (passive, with $\langle\zeta^{2}\rangle \le 1$) needs a deposit correlated over more than $460$ (at $1$ MeV) to $6.8 \times 10^{17}$ (at $10^{12}$ GeV) Hubble lengths of the descent, one comoving length (about $9.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the present Hubble radius) at every reheating temperature, initial data of the pre-metric sector.

entities.title: Under (F), the frozen point reads the descent deposit as vacuum
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: Under hypothesis (F) (the late de Sitter stage is the frozen point's own field), a deposit correlated by the frozen point's stabiliser invariant $Z$ reaches $|x_{d}| = \eta_{\infty} - \eta_{d}$, $a_{0}H_{0}|x_{d}| \in (4.32, 4.34)$, which exceeds the required range ($a_{0}H_{0}R_{\mathrm{req}} \approx 9.5 \times 10^{-6}$, one length for every $T_{d}$) by over $4 \times 10^{5}$; but with $k_{*}|x_{d}| \in (960, 968)$ every observed mode is inside the frozen point's horizon at the descent, so the invariant (Euclidean) state of every unitary-series field, and the massless Bunch-Davies state, give the vacuum's $n_{s} - 1 = 2$ up to $O(u^{-2})$, more than $480$ standard deviations from the measured value: range is not the obstruction, horizon exit is.

entities.title: Dating the descent
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: The Dirac coincidence is automatic in a $\Lambda$-dominated era; under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion, which the series adopts, the descent froze at the origin with $N$ and $v/H$ initial data and $v/M_{P}$ the law, and the descent could seed the measured spectrum only through a pre-metric deposit correlated over hundreds to $10^{18}$ of its Hubble lengths or a later source, neither of which the series supplies.

entities.title: A quasi-free deposit is the vacuum plus shot noise
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: For every quasi-free state of a CAR algebra and every bilinear observable, $\mathrm{sd}_{\omega}(O) \le \mathrm{sd}_{\omega_{0}}(O) + \Tr(F^{2}X)^{1/2}$ with $X = (\Gamma - \Gamma_{0})^{2} + \Gamma(1 - \Gamma)$, $\Tr X = 2\omega(N_{0})$: if a deposit is quasi-free it is the vacuum plus shot noise whatever its correlation range or partner placement, and the descent's parity average adds a region-independent constant; for the I-state, or any occupation profile with at least one thermal species' number of quanta and energy spread $c_{k} \le 1.31$, the shot term at the pivot is below $10^{-77}$ for every reheating temperature, far below $A_{s} = 2.1 \times 10^{-9}$, while a sparse or energetically broad deposit is bounded only by $(3c_{k}k^{3}/2\pi^{2}\bar n)^{1/2}$.

entities.title: A Kasner approach gives horizon exit with index three and no red tilt
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: On a Kasner approach ($\sum p_{j} = 1$, hidden directions and points inside the circle included), within one epoch, a massless minimally coupled scalar's mode along a principal axis obeys Bessel's equation of order $0$ in $s = k\tau^{1-p}/(1-p)$, so modes leave the Hubble length but the exited spectrum is $k^{3}$ times a squared logarithm, index in $[2, 3]$ and above $2.57$ once a hundred times outside: no red tilt; it has the same leading power $k^{3}$ as a finite-range deposit, enhanced by a squared logarithm, so it is not of finite range.

entities.title: The Hadamard condition leaves the deposit spectrum free on bounded bands
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: Relative to any homogeneous Hadamard reference state a homogeneous deposit can have any spectrum on any bounded band of scales; for the conformally coupled field a power-law ratio holds on no band unbounded toward short scales, and, for slice fields of nonzero mean, a red law on no band reaching k = 0, so a red band needs two ends that the Hadamard condition does not fix.

entities.title: Kasner coupled modes reach the measured tilt only by a fitted coupling
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: On a Kasner approach ($\sum P = 1$) the gravitational field's off-diagonal modes obey Bessel's equation of order $|P_{a} - P_{b}|/(1 - P_{j})$ and a curvature-coupled scalar order $\sqrt{\xi}|c|/(1 - P_{j})$, so red strain spectra exit, but with indices spreading by at least $4$ between axes on the vacuum circle; with equal observed exponents the Kaluza-Klein vector's transverse potential has index $(5 - 11p)/(1 - p)$ in $[-1, 3]$ (gauge-invariant at linear order) but its field strength has index $5 - 2\nu \in [1, 5]$, blue, and a curvature-coupled scalar matches the measured tilt only for $\xi \in [1.5225, 1.5481]$, a coupling fitted to it that nothing in the series fixes.

entities.title: Red-tilt criterion on power-law stages and the index ledger of the stored mode equations
entities.subject: dark-energy
entities.one_liner: Given the stored index $3 - 2\nu$, a mode obeying $\ddot\chi + (1 + f)\dot\chi/T + (k^{2}T^{-2P} - \kappa T^{-2})\chi = 0$ is red exactly when $f^{2} + 4\kappa > 9(1 - P)^{2}$; for a minimally coupled field on an isotropic power law this is $p > \tfrac23$, which the unit trace of every stored wall excludes; the stored hidden-scale, Kaluza-Klein, tree-level curvature and de Sitter rows all miss the measured index or reach it only through a chosen number (the Kaluza-Klein potential at the vacuum end $p = \tfrac12$ is red with none, index $-1$); the list of rows is argued complete from a search; and under the hypothesis of a contracting dust stage with the frozen point's constant, which the store does not hold, the spectrum depends on $k$ through $\Lambda A^{2}/k^{6}$ only, so a tilt with $G'(0) \ne 0$ carries a running of $-6$ times the index.
